history.period: About 200 years old (early 19th century, per myadhyatm.com)
history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE - GENERIC NAME: 'Shiv Mandir' is too generic to identify uniquely in Hoshiarpur district, which has many Shiva shrines. This entry documents the BEST-SUPPORTED referent: the Prachin Panchmukhi Shiv Mandir (Shimla hill / Ajjowal area, Hoshiarpur city), the only Hoshiarpur 'Shiv Mandir' with a dedicated article and detailed web coverage (myadhyatm.com). It is a ~200-year-old Shiva temple where the deity is worshipped in Panchmukhi (five-faced) form; the temple doors open at 4 AM daily for shringaar and abhishek with bilva leaves, hemp, milk, lassi, dhatura, akshat and sandalwood paste; 450-500 devotees visit daily; the month of Sawan brings special Jalabhishek and a closing Bhandara; Ram Darbar holds sankirtan 7:30-8 PM daily. Besides the Panchmukhi Shivalinga, the complex houses idols of Ram Darbar, Hanuman, Santoshi Mata, Parshuram, Lakshmi Narayan, Saraswati, Durga, Kali, Radha-Krishna, Ganesha, Nandi, Sheetala Mata, Shani Dev and Bhairava. Priest lineage: Pandit Karmchand served the temple 1953-1990; his son Vijay Kumar continues the sewa. ALTERNATIVE CANDIDATES the CSV could intend (documented, NOT conflated here): (1) Bhutgiri Shiv Mandir on Unna Road, Hoshiarpur - said to have been built in 1902 by Mistry Bholaram after a Brahmin's counsel, blessed with a child thereafter (local tradition, weakly sourced); (2) Prachin Shiv Mandir Gagan Ji Ka Tilla near Dasuya - an ancient hill shrine with 750+ steps, famed for its Mahashivratri fair. RECOMMENDATION: confirm with the dataset owner which shrine 'Shiv Mandir' refers to; the entry should be re-titled if it is one of the others.

name: Shiv Mandir
town: Hoshiarpur (CSV town correct - the documented Panchmukhi Shiv Mandir is in Hoshiarpur city, Ajjowal / Shimla hill area)
town_description: Hoshiarpur is a historic city of Punjab's Doaba region in the Shivalik foothills, known for its archaeological museum, Sheesh Mahal, Kamahi Devi temple, the Gagan Ji Ka Tilla shrine, and Sikh shrines including Gurdwara Harian Velan (~11 km away) and Gurdwara Bhai Joga Singh in Mohalla Shekhon. It lies on the Hoshiarpur-Chandigarh road, about 140 km from Chandigarh and ~45-70 km from the Kangra valley Shaktipeeths of Himachal Pradesh.

travel.airport: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport, Amritsar (~140 km); Chandigarh International Airport (~140 km).
travel.railway: Hoshiarpur railway station (small station; Jalandhar City ~40 km is the nearest major railhead). Auto-rickshaw to Ajjowal / Shimla hill area within the city.
travel.road: Hoshiarpur is on the Hoshiarpur-Chandigarh road (NH 503); the temple is within Hoshiarpur city in the Ajjowal / Shimla hill locality, reachable by auto-rickshaw.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Sawan month (July-August) is the most devotionally active period.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Doors open from 4:00 AM daily (per myadhyatm.com; closing time unverified).
